title: JarvisBench: Always-on Intelligence Between Humans and Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.14870v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long-horizon agents can execute continuously, but human attention remains intermittent and scarce. This creates a bidirectional coordination problem: users may need immediate access to an agent while work continues in the background, whereas agents may encounter consequential decisions that require user judgment after the user has stopped monitoring execution. We posit an always-on attention-coordination layer---\textit{Jarvis}\footnote{Named after the fictional AI assistant in \textit{Iron Man}.}---that mediates this interface and allocates human attention across one or more working agents. We introduce \textit{JarvisBench} to evaluate both directions of this coordination: whether an intermediary can accurately and promptly answer user-initiated questions about ongoing work, and whether it can recognize when an agent requires user judgment, solicit that judgment at the right moment, and route it back to improve task outcomes. translated_title: JarvisBench：人类与智能体之间的常驻智能协调
translated_abstract: 摘要：长期运行的智能体可以持续执行任务，但人类的注意力仍然是间歇性的且稀缺的。这产生了一个双向协调问题：当后台工作继续进行时，用户可能需立即访问智能体；而智能体可能在用户停止监控执行后，遇到需要用户判断的关键决策。我们提出一个常驻的注意力协调层——\textit{Jarvis}\footnote{以《钢铁侠》中的虚构AI助手命名。}——它作为这一界面的中介，并在一个或多个工作智能体之间分配人类注意力。我们引入\textit{JarvisBench}来评估这种协调的两个方向：中介能否准确且及时地回答用户对进行中工作的提问，以及它能否识别智能体何时需要用户判断，在合适的时机征求该判断，并将其反馈以改善任务结果。
tldr: 本文提出了JarvisBench，一个评估常驻注意力协调层在人类与长期运行智能体之间双向协调（用户提问响应和智能体请求判断）能力的基准。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces JarvisBench, a benchmark for evaluating an always-on attention-coordination layer's bidirectional coordination between humans and long-horizon agents, covering both user-initiated queries and agent-initiated judgment requests.
